message.content:
**Hydrogen (H)** – the simplest and most abundant element in the universe – has a range of distinctive physical and chemical properties:

| Property | Value / Description |
|----------|---------------------|
| **Atomic number** | 1 |
| **Atomic mass** | ~1.008 u (average; varies with isotope) |
| **Electron configuration** | 1s¹ |
| **Electronegativity (Pauling scale)** | 2.20 |
| **First ionization energy** | 13.598 eV (1312 kJ/mol) |
| **Second ionization energy** | 27.211 eV (2625 kJ/mol) |
| **Electron affinity** | 0.754 eV (77 kJ/mol) |
| **Boiling point** | –252.87 °C (20.28 K) at 1 atm |
| **Melting point** | –259.16 °C (14.01 K) at 1 atm |
| **Density at STP** | 0.08988 g/L (≈0.0000899 kg/m³) |
| **Molar volume at STP** | 22.414 L/mol |
| **State at room temperature** | Gas |
| **Flammability** | Extremely flammable; forms explosive mixtures with air (range 4–75 % H₂ in air) |
| **Isotopes** | Protium (^1H), Deuterium (^2H, D), Tritium (^3H, T) |
| **Bonding** | Forms covalent bonds; diatomic molecules (H₂) under normal conditions |
| **Reactivity** | Highly reactive; reacts with halogens, oxygen, metals, and many other elements; forms hydrides (ionic or covalent) |
| **Solubility in water** | Low (~0.0016 mol/L at 25 °C) |
| **Acidity/Basicity** | Acts as a weak acid when dissolved in water (forming hydronium ions) |
| **Spectral lines** | Prominent Balmer series in visible spectrum; Lyman series in ultraviolet |
| **Applications** | Fuel cell technology, rocket propellant, industrial hydrogenation, laboratory reagent, medical imaging (tritium labeling) |

### Key Points

- **Lightest Element:** With only one proton and one electron, hydrogen is the lightest element, giving it unique kinetic properties (high diffusion rates).
- **Isotopic Variants:** Deuterium and tritium have additional neutrons, affecting nuclear reactions and providing useful tracers in scientific research.
- **Energy Carrier:** Hydrogen’s high specific energy makes it attractive for clean fuel applications, though storage and safety remain challenges.
- **Chemical Behavior:** As a nonmetal, hydrogen typically forms covalent bonds, but it can also act as an acidic proton donor or form ionic hydride species with highly electropositive metals.

These properties make hydrogen a cornerstone of both fundamental chemistry and emerging technologies.
